Definition: from G4177 ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a community:--commonwealth, freedom.
BiblicalUsage: Politeia is citizenship, and Paul uses it twice in two very different ways. In one place he has bought his Roman citizenship with a great sum, and in the other he tells Gentile believers they were once strangers to the commonwealth of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws the line between belonging and being shut out, and the gospel moves that line so that strangers become fellow citizens.
